metadata.title: PG1000- Bacon Wrapped Hot Dogs with Baked Beans
metadata.description: Cookshack's Continuous Improvement Manager, Butch Flick uses the Fast Eddy's™ by Cookshack PG1000 pellet grill to make bacon wrapped hot dogs for National Hot Dog month. The different zones of the pellet grill allow you to sear on the direct side and smoke on the indirect side.

nodes.plm_caption: This video is an advertisement for the company Cookshack. The video shows a bald-headed, white man dressed in black t-shirt and blue latex gloves in front of a red table, a silver cutting board, and several hot dogs and bacon on it. The man introduces the recipe to his audience, which is called 'Bacon-Wrapped Hot Dogs' while putting hot dogs with bacon wrapped around them into a large smoking machine using wooden toothpicks. The hot dogs are moved into the smoker and cooked until the hot dogs and beans are ready to be served to the audience and the man is seen serving the hot dogs with the beans on the side. The video ends with text and a phone number displayed on the screen.

summary.brief: A bald chef wraps hot dogs in bacon, cooks them on a pellet grill with baked beans, and serves the finished meal.
summary.detailed: The video begins with a title slide and then shows a bald white man in a black shirt and blue latex gloves standing behind a red‑cloth‑covered table that holds a white cutting board, hot dogs, bacon, wooden toothpicks and a can of Bush's grilled beans. He explains the recipe, wraps each hot dog with a slice of bacon, secures the wrap with a toothpick, and places the dogs on a pre‑heated Cookshack PG1000 pellet grill set to 375 °F. After a brief two‑minute sear on the direct side, he moves the dogs to the indirect side to finish cooking for about 20‑30 minutes while an aluminum pan of baked beans warms on the top shelf. He then removes the toothpicks, plates the hot dogs in buns, adds ketchup, cheddar cheese and chili, and serves the beans on the side. The segment ends with several white screens displaying the Cookshack logo, website addresses and a phone number.

action.brief: Prepare and cook bacon‑wrapped hot dogs

summary.brief: Bacon‑wrapped hot dogs are wrapped, secured, smoked with baked beans, then plated with toppings.
summary.detailed: The segment opens with a title/loading screen displaying the Cookshack logo and contact information. A man in a black shirt and blue gloves stands behind a red‑cloth‑covered table with a white cutting board, hot dogs, strips of bacon, a cup of toothpicks, a can of baked beans and an aluminum foil pan. He pulls a hot dog from the board, wraps a slice of bacon around it and inserts a toothpick to hold the bacon in place. After the PG1000 pellet smoker is pre‑heated to 375 °F, he pours the canned baked beans into the foil pan, stirs them, and places the pan on the top (indirect) shelf of the smoker. He then places the bacon‑wrapped hot dogs on the lower (direct) shelf, sears each side briefly with metal tongs, and moves them to the indirect side to finish cooking for about 20–30 minutes until the bacon is crisp. Once cooked, he removes the toothpicks, lifts the hot dogs and beans from the smoker, and plates them, topping two hot dogs with ketchup and shredded cheddar cheese while serving the beans (and a side of chili) alongside. The segment ends with a series of Cookshack promotional graphics showing the website, phone number and a red flame logo.

summary.brief: A man wraps bacon around hot dogs, grills them with baked beans on a pellet grill, and plates the finished dish.
summary.detailed: The segment opens with a loading screen that displays the Cookshack website and phone number. A man wearing a black shirt and blue latex gloves appears behind a red‑cloth‑covered table holding a white cutting board, several hot dogs, strips of bacon, a cup of toothpicks and an aluminum foil pan. He slides a strip of bacon over each hot dog, twists it into a tight spiral and secures it with a toothpick. He then scoops canned baked beans into the foil pan, stirs them with a spatula and sets the pan on the top shelf of a pre‑heated PG1000 pellet grill whose digital display reads around 375 °F. The wrapped hot dogs are placed on the lower grate; he flips them with metal tongs, moves them briefly to direct heat for a couple of minutes per side, and then returns them to indirect heat for about twenty minutes until the bacon is crisp. After cooking, he removes the toothpicks, lifts the hot dogs and beans off the grill, and plates the dogs in buns, topping them with ketchup and shredded cheddar cheese while serving the baked beans on the side. The segment ends with on‑screen graphics showing the Cookshack web address and phone number.

action.brief: Wrap, grill, and plate bacon‑wrapped hot dogs with baked beans
action.detailed: Wrap each hot dog with a strip of bacon, secure it with a toothpick, place a foil pan of baked beans on the top shelf of the pre‑heated PG1000 pellet grill set to about 375 °F, arrange the wrapped dogs on the lower grate, flip them and cook on indirect heat for about twenty minutes (briefly searing on direct heat for two minutes per side), then remove the toothpicks and serve the dogs in buns topped with ketchup and shredded cheddar cheese alongside the beans.

summary_sent_to_llm.title: PG1000- Bacon Wrapped Hot Dogs with Baked Beans
summary_sent_to_llm.description: Cookshack's Continuous Improvement Manager, Butch Flick uses the Fast Eddy's™ by Cookshack PG1000 pellet grill to make bacon wrapped hot dogs for National Hot Dog month. The different zones of the pellet grill allow you to sear on the direct side and smoke on the indirect side.
summary_sent_to_llm.root_summary: The video begins with a title slide and then shows a bald white man in a black shirt and blue latex gloves standing behind a red‑cloth‑covered table that holds a white cutting board, hot dogs, bacon, wooden toothpicks and a can of Bush's grilled beans. He explains the recipe, wraps each hot dog with a slice of bacon, secures the wrap with a toothpick, and places the dogs on a pre‑heated Cookshack PG1000 pellet grill set to 375 °F. After a brief two‑minute sear on the direct side, he moves the dogs to the indirect side to finish cooking for about 20‑30 minutes while an aluminum pan of baked beans warms on the top shelf. He then removes the toothpicks, plates the hot dogs in buns, adds ketchup, cheddar cheese and chili, and serves the beans on the side. The segment ends with several white screens displaying the Cookshack logo, website addresses and a phone number.

llm.system_prompt:
You evaluate YouTube videos for a video-understanding benchmark.

You will be given an Action100M-style summary of one video: title, description,
a hierarchical GPT-written summary of the whole video, and a deduplicated list
of action labels extracted at multiple levels of the video.

Your job is to judge:

1) DOMAINS — does this video clearly belong to any of these target domains?
   - "kitchen": a person preparing food in a kitchen-like setting
     (cooking, baking, food prep — NOT eating reviews, NOT pet-food prep,
     NOT food-product unboxing, NOT restaurant vlogs).
   - "manipulation": a person performing hand-object manipulation tasks
     with clear physical goals: assembly/disassembly, repair, crafting,
     tool use, packing, sorting. The video must show clear procedural
     manipulation, NOT just incidental hand movement (e.g. a vlog where
     someone holds things while talking does NOT count).
   - "navigation": the camera moves through a physical environment as an
     agent traverses space — first-person walking tours (museum, store,
     home, city street), driving / cycling / hiking POV footage, drone
     fly-throughs of indoor or outdoor scenes, room/house walkthroughs.
     The camera's translation through the environment IS the main content.
     Does NOT count: a stationary tripod with someone talking; a tutorial
     filmed in one place; b-roll where the camera only pans or zooms but
     does not translate; sports footage where the player moves but the
     camera stays put.
   A video can match zero, one, or multiple domains. Be strict — when in
   doubt, say "neither".

2) NUM_DISTINCT_EVENTS — count the number of *semantically distinct*
   sub-events (procedural steps) you see in the action list. Merge
   paraphrases of the same step into one. Ignore generic narration steps
   like "speak to camera" or "display title".

3) IS_GOOD_CANDIDATE — true only if BOTH:
   - at least one target domain matches
   - num_distinct_events > 3 (the video shows a real multi-step procedure)

Always return strict JSON in the requested schema.
